headline: The Auto Mechanic Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet customers, give times and shop quantities, describe a car's condition, ask simple questions and make polite requests at the shop, and start Auto Mechanic Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Greet customers and coworkers and pronounce key shop words like carro, llanta and llave.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr, the written accent, and greetings

words.note: rr is a strong trill: CA-rro. A single r between vowels is a quick tap.
ll sounds like English y: YAN-ta.
Also means key. ll sounds like y: YA-ve.
Short, pure vowels: GA-to. Also means cat.
ch sounds like English ch in church.
j sounds like a strong English h: ca-HUE-la. Common Mexican word.
Say every vowel: a-SEI-te.
The written accent marks the stress: ba-te-RÍ-a.
Stress falls on the last syllable: ta-YER.
A woman is la mecánica.

words.en: Good morning, my name is Carlos.
Nice to meet you, I'm the mechanic.
words.note: A woman says: soy la mecánica.
Formal usted: use it with customers.
To a woman: bienvenida.

lessons.speaking: Greet a customer at the counter, say your name and that you are the mechanic, and welcome them to the shop.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Say times, counts and shop quantities like quarts, PSI and socket sizes.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time (a las 8:30), and shop units: quarts, gallons, PSI, inches

words.note: Common US shop word; read it from the odometer.
In the US, oil is sold by the quart.
For tire pressure, libras means PSI.
Say the system: de 10 milímetros or de media pulgada.

words.en: According to the manual, it takes 5 quarts of oil.
words.es: Según el manual, lleva 5 cuartos de aceite.
words.note: Oil capacity varies by vehicle; always check the manual.

words.es: La etiqueta de la puerta dice 35 libras.
words.note: Tire pressure varies by vehicle; read the door label.

words.en: The tire is missing 2 lug nuts.
I'll be back in half an hour.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker the appointment time, how many quarts the manual lists, and the PSI on the door sticker.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Say what a car or part is and describe its condition or location with ser and estar.
lessons.focus: ser for what something is, estar for its condition or location

words.note: Some shops also say la rampa.
Mexican usage; other regions say el capó.
estar: a condition that can change.
The adjective matches: la llanta gastada, el tornillo gastado.

words.en: The car is on the lift.
words.es: El carro está en el elevador.
words.note: estar for location.
ser: what something is. Troca is common US and Mexican usage.

lessons.speaking: Describe a car on the lift to a coworker: say what it is and whether the oil is low or a tire is worn.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what you have, need and want, what there is, and what you must do in the shop.
lessons.focus: tener, hay, necesitar, querer and hay que + infinitive

words.note: Mexican usage; other regions say el destornillador.
Mexican usage; many US shops also say la parte.

words.en: Do you have the car keys?
There's a noise in the front tire.
words.es: Hay un ruido en la llanta delantera.
words.note: hay: there is / there are.

words.en: The customer wants an oil change.
words.es: La clienta quiere un cambio de aceite.
words.note: A woman is la clienta; a man is el cliente.

words.en: You have to wear safety glasses.
words.es: Hay que usar lentes de seguridad.
words.note: hay que + infinitive: something everyone must do.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker what tools you need, what the customer wants, and what everyone has to wear in the shop.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Say where you are going, what you're going to do, and what you can do in the shop.
lessons.focus: ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer and poder

words.note: Mexican usage; can mean now or in a little while.

words.en: I'm going to the parts store.
words.es: Voy a la tienda de refacciones.

words.en: I'm going to check the brakes today.
words.es: Voy a revisar los frenos hoy.
words.note: ir a + infinitive: a plan.

words.en: Can I move your car to the parking lot?
She's going to wait in the waiting room.
words.es: Ella va a esperar en la sala de espera.

lessons.speaking: Tell the shop foreman where you are going, what you are going to do today, and what you can do tomorrow.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Describe everyday shop tasks in the present tense with yo, tú, usted, nosotros and ellos.
lessons.focus: Present tense of regular -ar, -er, -ir verbs: yo, tú, usted, nosotros, ellos

words.note: Common shop word for an engine belt.
-ar verbs: cambio, cambias, cambia, cambiamos, cambian.

words.en: I write the mileage on the receipt.
words.es: Yo escribo el millaje en el recibo.

words.note: tú: informal, between coworkers.

words.en: You pick up your car at 5.
words.es: Usted recoge su carro a las 5.
words.note: usted: formal, for customers.
-ir verbs: abro, abres, abre, abrimos, abren.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker what you do each day in the shop, and ask what they check on a car.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask customers and coworkers simple questions about a car, its owner, cost and timing.
lessons.focus: Question words: qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué, cuál

words.note: It matches the noun: ¿cuántos carros?, ¿cuántas llantas?
Two words in questions; porque (one word) means because.
Use ¿cuál es...? for 'what is' a name or number.

words.en: What problem does your car have?
How much does the oil change cost?
Who is the owner of the car?

lessons.speaking: Ask a customer what problem the car has, when the noise starts, who the owner is, and their phone number.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say no, never, nobody, nothing and not yet, and compare with more, less and another.
lessons.focus: no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos and otro

words.note: After a verb, keep no: No veo nada.
Never use un before otro: otro trapo.

words.es: Su carro todavía no está listo.
No hay nadie en la oficina.

words.en: I never work under the car without jack stands.
words.es: Nunca trabajo debajo del carro sin soportes de seguridad.
words.note: Some shops call jack stands las torres.

words.en: I don't see anything under the car.
words.es: No veo nada debajo del carro.

lessons.speaking: Tell a customer their car isn't ready yet, that you see no leak under it, and that another tire costs less.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Make polite requests and give simple usted commands to customers at the shop.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede…? requests and usted commands for everyday shop verbs

words.en: Can you turn off the engine, please?
words.note: ¿Puede + infinitive? is a polite request to one person.

words.en: Put on the parking brake, please.
words.es: Ponga el freno de mano, por favor.
words.note: Usted command: poner becomes ponga.

words.en: Can you give me your name?

lessons.speaking: Ask a customer politely to turn off the engine, put on the parking brake, and sign at the counter.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Recognize shop cognates and use survival phrases to get help when you don't understand.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad and -ente, plus survival phrases

words.note: -ción words are feminine: la inspección.
-dad words are feminine and match English -ty.
A woman is la clienta.

words.en: I don't understand, can you repeat?
How do you say 'lug nut' in Spanish?
I need help with the repair.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker you speak a little Spanish, ask them to repeat more slowly, and ask how to say a part in Spanish.
